title: Whole Milk 1 gal

drivers.name: Price increase (5.1% above regular)
drivers.evidence: Two past weeks at $4.56: average 202.6 units vs baseline 207.6 → x0.975; adjusted for noise, x0.89. Apply to median: 207.6 × 0.89 = 184.8.

drivers.name: Supplier delivery short warning
drivers.evidence: No past occurrence of delivery issues; only one warning. Shrink toward 1.0. Add downside risk: credible but untested. Adjust by -5%.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 207.6. No events are scheduled. The price is 5.1% above regular, which historically correlates with lower demand: past 4.56 price weeks (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) averaged x0.89 vs baseline. The supplier warning of short delivery suggests potential stockout risk, which may reduce sales. This is a single data point, so shrink effect toward 1.0. The classical model suggests no uplift, but the price increase and supply risk justify a downward adjustment. Noise-adjusted price effect is x0.89; supply risk adds uncertainty. Combine multiplicatively and shrink. No promotion or holiday drivers. The 5%-95% range should widen slightly due to uncertainty.

  median 207.6 | 5%-95%: 133.3 - 290.5 | 10%-90%: 156.2 - 281.3

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-22% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
